source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability with Sparse Autoencoder Neural Operators
source.authors: Bahareh Tolooshams; Ai-Zhong Shen; Anima Anandkumar

record.file_problem: The full paper text and appendices are present. Some extracted figure labels and equations are garbled, but the relevant discussion and figure descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures learned dictionary-atom correlations and how concept structure varies with sparsity. It argues that functional SAE parameterization can learn correlated concepts, refining the idea that learned features are necessarily nearly orthogonal. It does not reproduce the original toy-model experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on image-data SAEs and synthetic signals, not language-model internal activations. Rows below cover reported pairwise-correlation, Hoyer-structure, and moving-digit concept-stability results. Reconstruction, throughput, and other results are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions. The correlation and stability values are shown in figures without exact numeric values; only the authors' textual descriptions are used to determine state.
record.test_reason: The SAEs are trained directly on image pixels and synthetic signals, not on any network's internal activations. The results compare the authors' SAE-FNO against SAE-MLP and SAE-CNN baselines on dictionary geometry, concept stability, utilization and reconstruction. Nothing measures how a trained network stores features, so V1 (toy-network superposition geometry) and V5 (SAE features as the model's units) are not tested. The paper cites the near-orthogonality picture as SAE-MLP's inductive bias and builds a method that relaxes it; this is the study's own method compared with baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that functional (Fourier) parameterization with concept and domain sparsity lets SAEs encode how and where concepts are expressed. They report SAE-FNO learns more structured, stable and efficient concepts, with a broader range of concept correlations. They also report it generalizes across discretizations, and that lifting acts as a preconditioner. They stress the experiments are on vision data directly, not on internal model representations.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of Toy Models of Superposition. It trains and analyzes sparse autoencoders on structured image and synthetic data, using Fourier neural operators and feature-map concepts, rather than testing the original toy-network setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported concept structure changes with concept-sparsity level for SAE-MLP but is described as stable for SAE-FNO; SAE-CNN structure also depends on kernel size. SAE-FNO correlation results are shown across different concept-sparsity settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On raw-pixel MNIST and CIFAR, SAE-MLP dictionary atoms have pairwise cosine similarities concentrated near zero. SAE-FNO atoms show a broader, heavier-tailed distribution. This is shown in figures only (Figs 14 and 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How near-orthogonal an SAE's learned dictionary is depends on the SAE's parameterization (vector versus functional/convolutional), not only on the data.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-MLP atom structure (Hoyer score) and identity consistency against a k = 50 anchor change sharply as k varies, while SAE-FNO stays stable (Figs 10, 12, 13, 35). Under translation, SAE-MLP swaps active concepts while SAE-FNO keeps IoU near 1 (Fig 38). All results are on pixel-level SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which SAE features are learned, and how stable they are across sparsity settings and input translations, depends on the SAE's architecture and hyperparameters.

record.problems: The empirical study focuses on vision and synthetic data, not LLM representations or the original toy-network setting. Correlation and Hoyer results relevant here are chiefly figure-based and do not provide exact plotted values in the text. Pairwise atom cosine similarity is a geometric measure, not a direct measurement of behavioral interference.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing directly on the listed versions were left out. Other reported reconstruction, utilization, runtime, discretization-generalization, and lifting results do not measure these claim versions.

untested.parts: All parts. No small network is trained to store sparse features in fewer dimensions, and no superposition geometry or sparsity transition is measured.
All parts. There are no LLM or other model activations; SAEs are trained on raw images.
All parts. SAE features are not extracted from a model, so whether they are the model's units is not addressed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked SAE dictionary geometry on raw pixels to V1 and own-method concept stability to V5. Neither measures a network's internal features, so all rows are relinked to none. The study cites Toy Models only to motivate the near-orthogonality bias of standard SAEs. The reader's labels (supports, limits_scope, challenges) are dropped.

versions.untested_parts: Does not reproduce the original toy-model setup or establish a sparsity-dependent transition in that setup; does not test feature importance. Tests learned SAE geometry and its relation to sparsity on image data.
No test of neurons becoming polysemantic from capacity competition, or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No LLM activations, multi-neuron feature analysis, or LLM SAE recovery.

Tests selected aspects of concept stability across sparsity and translated image inputs. Does not test completeness or canonicality of SAE features, or whether they are units of a model's internal representation.
Uses feature-map concepts, but does not test whether the features that are superposed in a network are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-MLP atom correlations on MNIST and CIFAR across the plotted concept-sparsity settings
reader_labels.reason: The authors say pairwise correlations are sharply concentrated near zero, consistent with near-orthogonal learned atoms (rows corr_mnist_k50_mlp through corr_mnist_k1000_mlp and corr_cifar_k10_mlp through corr_cifar_k700_mlp).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE-FNO atom correlations on MNIST and CIFAR across the plotted concept-sparsity settings
reader_labels.reason: SAE-FNO has broader correlation distributions with heavier tails than SAE-MLP, indicating that learned concepts need not be nearly orthogonal and that geometry depends on parameterization (rows corr_mnist_k50_fno through corr_mnist_k1000_fno and corr_cifar_k10_fno through corr_cifar_k700_fno).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE-FNO Hoyer structure across concept-sparsity levels on MNIST and CIFAR
reader_labels.reason: SAE-FNO's structural characteristics remain stable as concept sparsity changes, rather than showing a general sparsity-driven structural transition (rows hoyer_mnist_fno and hoyer_cifar_fno).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-MLP Hoyer structure across concept-sparsity levels on MNIST and CIFAR
reader_labels.reason: SAE-MLP's Hoyer-score distributions shift substantially with concept sparsity, showing sparsity-dependent changes in learned structure (rows hoyer_mnist_mlp and hoyer_cifar_mlp).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-FNO on independently processed translated MNIST frames, k = 10, 25, and 50
reader_labels.reason: SAE-FNO maintains a highly stable active concept set across consecutive frames, with reported IoU approximately 1 (rows moving_mnist_k10_fno, moving_mnist_k25_fno, moving_mnist_k50_fno).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: SAE-MLP on independently processed translated MNIST frames, k = 10, 25, and 50
reader_labels.reason: SAE-MLP rapidly swaps active concepts between frames, failing the tested temporal concept-stability aspect (rows moving_mnist_k10_mlp, moving_mnist_k25_mlp, moving_mnist_k50_mlp).
